revolutionary-battles-1775-1776.works: The three winner colors are strong and the legend words are short ('British Victory', 'American Victory', and 'Inconclusive' is close to Spanish 'inconcluso'). Every battle pop-up puts the name and the date on the first two lines, so I get the date without reading the long English story. The numbered white circles are easy to see, the Turning Point pop-up says 'Victor: Britain' in plain words, and the big circled anchor and the small anchor are easy to tell apart.

findings.where: q1-bookmark (Massachusetts bookmark): Revolutionary War Battles diamonds and Turning Points circles 1-2; Q1 steps 2, 4 and 5 (click Lexington and Concord, click Boston, measure Boston to Concord)
findings.what: The sheet says click the Lexington and Concord diamond and the Boston diamond, but nothing on the map says Boston, Lexington or Concord. I see a blue diamond, white circles 1 and 2, and another blue diamond on the coast. I have to click each one to find which is which, and circle 2 sits right on Boston, so I can't see if a diamond is under it. To measure Boston to Concord I don't know where to put the two points.
findings.why: She finds places by the English names the sheet gives her. With no town names and a circle covering the Boston spot she has to guess, and the measurement depends on picking the right two points.
findings.suggestion: Label the battle diamonds with a short name at the bookmark's zoom, or draw the Turning Points circles beside the diamonds instead of on top. On the sheet, say which shape is Boston (check which diamond opens the Boston pop-up) and that the Lexington and Concord diamond is the blue one just left of circle 1.

findings.where: q2-colony, q2-colony-ny, q2-bunkerhill: Thirteen British Colonies (Colony Area) and the basemap labels; Q2 step 3 (click the colony under each group of diamonds to read its name)
findings.what: I click inside Virginia and inside New York and nothing opens. Some colony names are written on the map, but the Boston battles have no name near them: 'Massachusetts' is written far up in the north (in Maine), and the nearest word to Boston is 'New Hampshire'. The New Jersey battles have no name at this zoom, and Rhode Island has none either.
findings.why: Doing exactly what the sheet says gives her nothing, so she thinks she did it wrong. Reading the nearest label, she may write New Hampshire for the Boston battles and miss New Jersey, which is the centre of the 1776 answer.
findings.suggestion: Turn on a one-line pop-up for Colony Area that shows the colony name, or label the colonies so the Massachusetts label sits near Boston and New Jersey and Rhode Island show at this zoom. If not, change the sheet to 'lee el nombre de la colonia escrito en el mapa (acércate si no aparece)' and note that Massachusetts then reached up into Maine.
findings.evidence: revolutionary-battles-1775-1776--q2-colony.png (no pop-up opened); revolutionary-battles-1775-1776--q2-colony-ny.png (no pop-up opened; 'Massachusetts' label in Maine; no New Jersey label); revolutionary-battles-1775-1776--q2-bunkerhill.png (no New Jersey label)

findings.where: q2-all and open: whole-map view with the legend open; Q2 step 1 (zoom out until you see every diamond from Quebec to South Carolina)
findings.what: When South Carolina is at the bottom of the screen, the Quebec diamond is off the top, and the legend box covers the north-east. In the first view Quebec shows but the Carolinas are cut off. If I zoom out once more the diamonds pile up.
findings.why: She can't check she has every diamond in one view, so she may leave Quebec or the Carolinas off her list of places.
findings.suggestion: Add a bookmark such as '1775-1776 all battles' framed from Quebec to Charleston at laptop size with the legend open, and name it in step 1 of the sheet.
findings.evidence: revolutionary-battles-1775-1776--q2-all.png (Quebec off the top); revolutionary-battles-1775-1776--open.png (Quebec shown, Carolinas off the bottom)

findings.where: Map layers list; Q3 step 1 (turn on Key Port Cities in the American Revolution 1775-1781, 'está dentro de Revolutionary War Battlefields')
findings.what: The sheet says Key Port Cities is inside Revolutionary War Battlefields. I open that group and only find 'Revolutionary War Core Areas' and 'Revolutionary War Battlefield Boundary'. Key Port Cities is on its own, second from the top of the list.
findings.why: She matches the long English layer names to the sheet carefully. When it isn't where the sheet says, she thinks the layer is missing.
findings.suggestion: Change the sheet to 'es la segunda capa de la lista, debajo de Turning Points' (or move the layer into the group if that was the plan).
findings.evidence: Map layers list in the packet: Key Port Cities is a top-level layer, second from top; Revolutionary War Battlefields holds only Core Areas and Battlefield Boundary

findings.where: q3-ports and q3-port: Key Port Cities layer and basemap; Q3 steps 3-4 (find the major ports between Boston and Charleston and name them from the coast and nearby battle diamonds)
findings.what: The sheet says the anchors have no pop-up, so I don't click them. The map has no city names here, only colony names. One big anchor sits right next to the New Jersey battle diamonds, so I would name it after that battle. The big anchor in Virginia has a blue diamond next to it but I don't know the city. When I click an anchor by accident, a pop-up opens with just the city name ('Stonington, CT'), which is the easiest English on the whole map.
findings.why: Naming ports from the coastline needs geography she may not have yet. The sheet's method points her to battle names, which are not port names, so she can write wrong answers, while the map already gives the name in one click.
findings.suggestion: Change step 4 to 'Haz clic en cada ancla: la ventana emergente da el nombre de la ciudad' and remove 'no tiene ventanas emergentes' from 'Cómo leer el mapa' and step 4. Check that the Major Port City anchors also show their name (only Stonington, a minor port, was tried).
findings.evidence: revolutionary-battles-1775-1776--q3-ports.png (no city labels; big anchor beside the New Jersey diamonds); revolutionary-battles-1775-1776--q3-port.png (pop-up 'Stonington, CT')

findings.where: q4-circles and q4-circle4: Turning Points circles 4 and 5 on top of Revolutionary War Battles diamonds; Q4 steps 2-4 (click Fort Washington, Fort Lee and Trenton, use the legend for the winner)
findings.what: I see circles 4 and 5 but no diamond under them. On the first map there was a blue diamond in New Jersey, but zoomed in, circle 5 is on that spot and the only diamond near it is red. Clicking circle 4 opens 'Battle Details' and '1 of 5', so I have to go through five English pop-ups with the arrows to find Fort Washington and Fort Lee.
findings.why: She may take the red diamond next to circle 5 for Trenton and write that Britain won. The diamond color is the only place the winner is shown, and the circle hides it.
findings.suggestion: Move the Turning Points circles off the diamonds, or draw them as a thin ring with no fill so the diamond color shows through; or add a 'Victor:' line to the battle pop-ups as Turning Points already has. On the sheet, say to click circle 5 and use the arrows ('1 of 5', as the app writes it) to find Trenton.
findings.evidence: revolutionary-battles-1775-1776--q4-circles.png; revolutionary-battles-1775-1776--q4-circle4.png ('1 of 5'); revolutionary-battles-1775-1776--open.png (blue diamond in New Jersey)

findings.where: q4-circles: basemap labels and the New York/New Jersey bookmark; Q4 steps 1 and 5 (zoom to New York City; measure New York City to Trenton)
findings.what: The sheet says zoom in on New York City, but there is a bookmark called New York/New Jersey that the sheet doesn't mention. Zoomed in, the map doesn't write New York City, Trenton, Fort Lee or even New Jersey, only Pennsylvania, Maryland and Delaware.
findings.why: Without names she doesn't know where to start and end the measurement. The bookmark would put her in the right place without searching.
findings.suggestion: Point the sheet to the bookmark: 'Abre el marcador (Bookmarks) New York/New Jersey'. Give the measuring points in map terms, e.g. 'desde el ancla grande de Nueva York hasta el círculo 5 (Trenton)'.

findings.where: q1-lexington and q2-bunkerhill: highlight on the clicked Revolutionary War Battles diamond; Q1 step 3, Q2 step 3, Q4 step 4 (use the legend to see who won)
findings.what: When I click a diamond it turns light blue while the pop-up is open, so I can't see if it was red or blue. Bunker Hill is a British win, but while selected it looks light blue, like 'American Victory'.
findings.why: The sheet makes the diamond color the only way to know the winner, and she reads the pop-up and the color at the same moment.
findings.suggestion: Set the highlight to an outline only so the fill color stays visible, or add 'Winner:' to the battle pop-ups. On the sheet: 'cierra la ventana para ver el color del rombo'.

findings.where: Q1 step 1 ('Abre el marcador Massachusetts'); the app's tool is called Bookmarks
findings.what: The sheet says 'marcador'. The tool in the app is 'Bookmarks'. For layers and measuring the sheet gives me the English word in brackets, but not for this one.
findings.why: She matches Spanish instructions to English buttons, and 'marcador' and 'Bookmarks' don't look alike.
findings.suggestion: Write 'Abre el marcador (Bookmarks) Massachusetts', as the sheet already does for Map layers and Measure.
findings.evidence: Student sheet Q1 step 1; tool list in the packet

roads-trails-and-rails-west.works: The legend gives each trail a short English name, the pop-up title tells me which trail I really clicked, and the railroad pop-up is one easy line ('Railroad in operation by: 1869'). When I zoom in, the nation names show on the map, some with the English name in brackets.

findings.where: q2-oregon: Trails West where several trails run together in Nebraska and Wyoming; Q2 step 2 (click the Oregon Trail, read its length and how many people used it), also Q1 step 2
findings.what: I click the line I think is the Oregon Trail and the pop-up says 'Pony Express Trail', '1 of 4'. Four trails are on top of each other there. I have to press the arrow and read each title until I find Oregon.
findings.why: The title shows her she got the wrong trail, which helps, but she has to page through long English pop-ups. If she misses the arrows she answers with the Pony Express numbers (10 days, 1,800 miles).
findings.suggestion: On the sheet, send her to a place where the Oregon Trail runs alone (in the opening view it runs by itself across Oregon), and write the counter as the app does ('1 of 4'). On the map, set the Trails West pop-up so the length and number of travellers come first.

findings.where: open and q3-indigenous: Trails West legend and lines; Q1 step 1 and Q2 step 1 (match each trail's color to the legend)
findings.what: Oregon and California are almost the same olive green. Mormon Pioneer, Old Spanish and Pony Express are all very dark dots (black, dark brown, dark red). Where the trails run together across Nebraska and Wyoming I can't tell which dots are which.
findings.why: The sheet sends her to the legend color first. When she can't match it, the only way left is clicking and paging through English pop-ups.
findings.suggestion: Give the trails colors that are further apart (for example green, gold, blue, red, purple, orange, brown) and/or label each trail with its name along the line.
findings.evidence: roads-trails-and-rails-west--open.png (legend swatches); roads-trails-and-rails-west--q3-indigenous.png (trails overlapping in Wyoming and Nebraska)

findings.where: Trails West pop-ups; Q2 step 2 (read the Oregon Trail's length and number of travellers)
findings.what: The Pony Express pop-up gives distances in kilometres first and miles in brackets. I didn't get to see the Oregon pop-up, so I don't know if it gives the length and the number of people in a short line I can find.
findings.why: Kilometres first may make her write km when the sheet compares it with a measurement in miles. If the Oregon numbers sit inside a long paragraph she may not find them.
findings.suggestion: Check that the Oregon Trail pop-up gives its length in miles and the number of travellers, and put each on its own short line near the top, miles first.
findings.evidence: roads-trails-and-rails-west--q2-oregon.png (Pony Express pop-up: '2897 kilometers (1,800 miles)'); the Oregon pop-up was not captured

findings.where: q2-oregon and open: basemap labels; Q2 steps 3-4 (find Independence next to Kansas City; measure Independence to Portland)
findings.what: I find Kansas City but no word 'Independence'. On the whole map I see Seattle and San Francisco but not Portland.
findings.why: She looks for the exact English word the sheet gives her. When it isn't there she isn't sure where to start or end the line.
findings.suggestion: On the sheet: 'Independence está justo al lado de Kansas City; si no ves el nombre, empieza en Kansas City' and 'acércate a Oregón para ver Portland'. Or add a small point layer for the trail start and end towns.
findings.evidence: roads-trails-and-rails-west--q2-oregon.png (Kansas City labelled, no Independence); roads-trails-and-rails-west--open.png (no Portland)

findings.where: q3-indigenous: Indigenous Territories under Trails West in Wyoming and Nebraska; Q3 steps 2-4 (zoom until names appear, follow a trail, find two nations whose land it crossed)
findings.what: The names do appear, but the colors overlap and I can't tell which name goes with which color. The trail goes through a grey-brown area and a yellow area that have no name I can see, while three names (Tséstho'e (Cheyenne), Oohenumpa, Sicangu) sit together in the blue area. Some color areas stop in straight lines, like boxes.
findings.why: She can copy a name, but she can't be sure the trail crosses that nation's land, and that is the evidence the question asks for.
findings.suggestion: Give Indigenous Territories a pop-up with the nation's name (and the English name where there is one), so clicking under the trail answers the question, and add thin outlines so overlapping areas can be told apart. Check on the live map whether the straight box edges are real or just tiles still loading.

findings.where: q4-railroads and q4-grayline: Railroads legend and Railroads 1826 to 1911; Q4 steps 2-3 (find Union Pacific and Central Pacific in the legend; click a thin grey line)
findings.what: The legend box is cut off: 'Transcontinental Railroad (Central Pacific)' is half hidden and Southern Pacific is below it, so I have to scroll inside the legend. The thin lines look black and crowded in the east, not grey. When I click a thin line in Wyoming the pop-up says 'Union Pacific (Transcontinental)', so I think I clicked the pink line by mistake.
findings.why: She checks the sheet's words against the map. 'Grey' lines that look black, and a grey-line pop-up with the transcontinental's name, make her doubt she did the step right.
findings.suggestion: On the sheet: 'líneas finas (grises o negras)', 'baja en la leyenda para ver Central Pacific', and 'la ventana puede dar el nombre de una compañía, como Union Pacific'. On the map, make the thin railroad lines a lighter grey so the colored transcontinental lines and the trails stand out.

us-slavery-and-slave-trade-1850.works: The colors match the sheet exactly: brown is free, green is slave, the light tones are 'by compromise', and the four tones are easy to tell apart. Each state pop-up has the name as its title and one sentence with the year, and at the bookmark the Underground Railroad cities are written in orange.

findings.where: open and q3-slavetrade: US States and Territories 1850 legend; Q1 step 1 (find the four groups)
findings.what: The legend box shows the line styles first. The four state groups are at the bottom and cut off, so I have to scroll. Under each group there is a long sentence like 'Free by Compromise of 1820, Missouri Compromise; Acts of Congress admitting Texas, Act of 1848, Ordinance of 1787, and state constitution', which I can't read. The group names ('Free states', 'Slave states', '... by compromise') I do understand.
findings.why: Q1 is about matching four colors to four groups. The long legal English hides the short group name she needs, and 'admitting Texas' under a free group can make her think Texas was free.
findings.suggestion: Shorten the legend labels to the group names ('Free state', 'Free by compromise', 'Slave state', 'Slave by compromise') and move the long source wording into the pop-ups. Put the states legend above the line layers so all four groups show without scrolling.

findings.where: q1-pennsylvania: US States and Territories 1850 pop-up; Q1 step 3 (read the year each state became free or slave)
findings.what: Pennsylvania's pop-up says 1780, then 'Abolition by state action between 1830-1850'. Which year do I write?
findings.why: She takes the pop-up words literally. Two different dates in one short pop-up block her answer.
findings.suggestion: Check the Pennsylvania record against the Harper's 1920 source and either fix the category or add a line explaining the difference. Also fix 'people 1780' to 'people in 1780'.
findings.evidence: Pop-up text: 'This state passed legislation against the enslavement of people 1780.' ... 'Abolition by state action between 1830-1850' (us-slavery-and-slave-trade-1850--q1-pennsylvania.png)

findings.where: q1-pennsylvania and q2-missouri: highlight on the clicked state; Q1 steps 2-3 (click one state from each group)
findings.what: When I click Pennsylvania, a free state, it turns blue-green, like the green of the slave states. Missouri turns bright turquoise.
findings.why: The whole key of the lesson is brown for free and green for slave, and the highlight paints a free state green while she is reading about it.
findings.suggestion: Set the highlight to an outline only (no fill), or to a color outside the brown and green scheme.

findings.where: q2-line: Missouri Compromise Line; Q2 step 2 (click the line and read its pop-up)
findings.what: I click on the grey dashed line and get 'Unorganized Territory', not the line. There is no '1 of 2' to find the line's own pop-up.
findings.why: She thinks she missed the line. She does get '1820' and 'Free by Missouri Compromise' from the territory, but the sheet told her to expect a pop-up for the line.
findings.suggestion: Check that the Missouri Compromise Line has its pop-up turned on and make the line wider so it is easy to click. If it has no pop-up, change the sheet to 'haz clic justo encima de la línea y lee el año en la ventana del territorio'.
findings.evidence: us-slavery-and-slave-trade-1850--q2-line.png; pop-up text 'Unorganized Territory ... in 1820 ... Free by Missouri Compromise'

findings.where: Internal Routes of the US Slave Trade legend; 'Cómo leer el mapa' and Q3
findings.what: The sheet says 'Amistad', but the legend says 'Route of L'Amistead'. I know 'amistad' from Spanish, but 'L'Amistead' looks like a different ship.
findings.why: She matches names letter by letter.
findings.suggestion: Rename the legend class to 'Route of La Amistad' (check the ship's name in a reliable source first).

findings.where: q4-bookmark (Illinois, Indiana, and Ohio): basemap; Q4 step 2 (follow the orange routes north from the Ohio River)
findings.what: The map doesn't write 'Ohio River' anywhere. I see a black line along the bottom of the brown states, but that is a slave trade route, not the river.
findings.why: She has to start from the river. Without a label she may start from the black slave-trade line or somewhere else.
findings.suggestion: On the sheet: 'el río Ohio es la frontera entre los estados marrones (libres) y los verdes (esclavistas)'. On the map, label the Ohio River at the bookmark's zoom.

findings.where: q4-bookmark: Underground Railroad Cities (black Canada dots) behind the legend panel; Q4 question '¿A dónde llevan las rutas?'
findings.what: The routes go up to Detroit and then under the legend box. I see half of one black dot ('Cha...'); the other Canada cities are hidden.
findings.why: The answer is the black dots in Canada, and with the legend open, as she has had it since Q1, she can't see them.
findings.suggestion: Move the bookmark extent east and north so Canada shows to the left of the legend, or add to the sheet 'cierra la leyenda y busca los puntos negros (Canadá)'.

findings.where: Q4 step 1 ('Abre el marcador Illinois, Indiana, and Ohio'); the app's tool is called Bookmarks
findings.what: The sheet says 'marcador', but the tool is 'Bookmarks'. The sheet gives the English for Map layers but not for this.
findings.why: She matches Spanish instructions to English buttons.
findings.suggestion: Write 'Abre el marcador (Bookmarks) Illinois, Indiana, and Ohio'.
findings.evidence: Student sheet Q4 step 1; tool list in the packet

civil-war-battlefields.works: State names are written on the map at the opening view, and the four state tones (dark blue, light blue, dark brown, light tan) are clearly different and fit the sheet's questions about before and after Fort Sumter. The battlefield pop-up is one short sentence with the name in capitals, and the battle pop-up shows the dates clearly.

findings.where: q3-railroads (states layer off, Virginia, North Carolina, Tennessee) and q2-dc: Railroads 1826 to 1863 (static); Q3 steps 2-3 (compare the railroads north and south of the boundary)
findings.what: I turn off the states layer and there are no dark grey railroad lines at all, only diamonds on the plain map. The legend has nothing for railroads. I only see thin dark lines when I zoom in much closer (around Antietam), and then I only see a small piece of the map.
findings.why: Q3 can't be answered: at a zoom where both sides of the boundary fit, there are no railroads to compare.
findings.suggestion: Check the visible range on 'Railroads 1826 to 1863 (static)' and set it to draw at the whole-country and regional views, and give it a legend entry ('Railroads by 1863'). If it can't draw there, the sheet must say how far to zoom in and to pan along the boundary.
findings.evidence: civil-war-battlefields--q3-railroads.png (no railroads); civil-war-battlefields--q2-dc.png (no railroads); civil-war-battlefields--q4-diamond.png (thin lines appear only at close zoom); legend text has no railroad entry

findings.where: q3-railroads: Boundary between Union and Confederacy with the states layer off; Q3 steps 1 and 3
findings.what: With the states turned off, the white dashed line almost disappears on the light map, and the state names go too. I can't tell which side is the Union.
findings.why: She needs the line to sort the railroads into Union and Confederate sides.
findings.suggestion: Draw the boundary darker (for example dark grey dashes with a white edge) so it shows on both the colored states and the plain basemap, or have the sheet make the states layer more transparent instead of turning it off.

findings.where: open and q2-dc: legend panel; Q1 steps 1-2, Q2 step 3, Q4 step 3
findings.what: The legend opens with the battle diamonds and the big casualty sizes. The state groups ('Union Free State', 'Slave state seceding before Fort Sumter, April 1861' ...) are cut off at the bottom, and I have to scroll inside the box.
findings.why: Three of the four questions need the state groups, and she may think the legend doesn't have them.
findings.suggestion: Put U.S. Civil War States and Territories (1863) first in the legend or make the casualty-size legend smaller; or add to the sheet 'baja en la leyenda hasta U.S. Civil War States and Territories (1863)'.

findings.where: U.S. Civil War States and Territories (1863) legend; Q1
findings.what: 'Slave state seceding before Fort Sumter, April 1861': I know 'before' and 'after', but 'seceding' is new to me.
findings.why: It is the key word in two of the four groups. The sheet says 'dejaron la Unión' and 'separarse' but never shows the English word.
findings.suggestion: On the sheet, add '(seceding = separándose de la Unión)' to Q1 step 1.
findings.evidence: Legend text in the packet; civil-war-battlefields--open.png

findings.where: q2-dc: state labels; Q2 steps 1-2 (zoom to Washington, D.C., find the two states around it)
findings.what: Zoomed in on D.C. I see 'District of Columbia', 'Virginia', 'West Virginia', 'Delaware' and 'New Jersey', but no 'Maryland'. Lots of diamonds are piled up around D.C.
findings.why: The question asks her to name the two states, and one name is missing at the zoom the sheet sends her to. It appears one zoom closer.
findings.suggestion: Make sure the Maryland label shows at this zoom, or add to the sheet 'acércate un poco más para ver Maryland'.

findings.where: q4-diamond and q4-gettysburg: United States Battlefield Boundaries over the states layer; Q4 steps 1-2 (zoom to Virginia, click the tan areas of two battlefields)
findings.what: The sheet says 'zonas color canela'. In Pennsylvania they are light grey shapes on dark blue and I can click Gettysburg. In Virginia the state itself is tan, so the battlefield areas almost vanish.
findings.why: The sheet sends her to Virginia first, and there she can't see what to click.
findings.suggestion: Give the battlefield areas a darker outline so they show on the tan Confederate states, and change the sheet's color word to what is drawn (for example 'gris claro').

findings.where: Total casualties legend (Civil War Battlefields)
findings.what: The smallest diamond says '< 0'. Less than zero soldiers?
findings.why: A number that can't be right makes her stop trusting the legend.
findings.suggestion: Relabel the smallest class as '< 10,000' (or whatever the real smallest class is).

the-battle-of-vicksburg.works: At the opening view, the yellow Vicksburg pin and the dark pins with bold English names are easy to find and match the sheet, and the railroad with cross marks is easy to follow from Vicksburg through Edwards to Jackson. The battle pop-ups put the name and date first, so the dates for Champion Hill and Port Hudson are easy to read.

findings.where: q1-bookmark (The Battle of Vicksburg bookmark): Key Places pins, Railroads 1826 to 1911, basemap; Q1 steps 3-4 and Q2 step 1
findings.what: After the bookmark I see Vicksburg, New Carthage, Hard Times and a pin at the bottom edge without a name. Milliken's Bend and Edwards are off the screen and Jackson is under the legend box. The sheet says 'acércate' to see the railroads, but I need to zoom out to see Jackson. East of Vicksburg the railroad runs right next to lines marked 'I-20' and 'Highway 80', and its little cross marks are hard to see. The opening map showed all of this better.
findings.why: She follows 'acércate' literally and ends up further from what she needs, and she may follow a highway instead of the railroad.
findings.suggestion: Reset the bookmark to the opening extent (Milliken's Bend to Jackson, with room for the legend), or change the sheet to 'aléjate un paso hasta ver Jackson'. Make the railroad line a little darker or thicker so it stands out from the basemap roads.

findings.where: Key Places in the Union March to Vicksburg labels; Q2 steps 1 and 3
findings.what: The sheet says 'Milliken's Bend', but the map writes 'Miliken's Bend', and it overlaps the basemap word 'Tallulah'.
findings.why: She matches names letter by letter and may think it is a different place.
findings.suggestion: Check the spelling and fix the label to 'Milliken's Bend', and move it off 'Tallulah'.

findings.where: open and q1-bookmark: Key Places pins along the Mississippi; Q2 step 2 (which side of the river is each pin)
findings.what: At the opening view Milliken's Bend and Bruinsburg Bend sit almost on the river, so I can't tell which side they are on. There are also dashed lines that wander away from the blue river, and I don't know if that is the river too.
findings.why: Which side each place is on is the point of Q2 (why Grant marched south before crossing).
findings.suggestion: On the sheet: 'acércate a cada alfiler; al oeste del río azul está Luisiana, al este Misisipi', and say what the dashed line is (check, it looks like the state border on an old river course). Or add the side to each pin's label or pop-up.
findings.evidence: the-battle-of-vicksburg--open.png; the-battle-of-vicksburg--q1-bookmark.png (dashed line away from the river)

findings.where: q3-battles: Civil War Battlefields legend; 'Cómo leer el mapa' and Q3
findings.what: Here 'Confederate Victory' is a grey diamond and 'Inconclusive' is yellow, the same yellow as the Vicksburg pin. 'Other' is a grey circle that looks like the grey diamond. In the Civil War Battlefields lesson, Confederate was brown.
findings.why: If she remembers the other lesson's colors she reads the wrong winner, and a yellow diamond next to the yellow pin looks like part of Vicksburg.
findings.suggestion: Use the same battle symbols as the Civil War Battlefields map (blue Union, brown Confederate, white Inconclusive) in every lesson.

findings.where: q4-porthudson: basemap labels; Q4 steps 1 and 4 (zoom out from Memphis to the Gulf; read the state names west of the river)
findings.what: Zoomed out at Port Hudson I see city names (Dallas, Houston, Shreveport, Baton Rouge, New Orleans) and 'Alabama', but no 'Louisiana', 'Texas' or 'Arkansas'. Memphis is off the top.
findings.why: The question asks which states are west of the river, and the basemap doesn't give their names at this zoom.
findings.suggestion: Add a bookmark 'Mississippi River: Memphis to the Gulf' at a zoom where the basemap shows the state names (check which zoom does), and name that bookmark on the sheet.

findings.where: q3-championhill and q4-porthudson: Civil War Battlefields pop-up
findings.what: Under the date there is a blue underlined 'Battlefield Trust page' and 'Tap on image to view page', but there is no image.
findings.why: It is extra English telling her to tap something that isn't there, and if she clicks the link she may leave the map.
findings.suggestion: Fix the image link in the pop-up, or replace it with a plain text link such as 'More about this battle (American Battlefield Trust)'.
findings.evidence: Pop-up text 'Battlefield Trust page / Tap on image to view page' (the-battle-of-vicksburg--q3-championhill.png; the-battle-of-vicksburg--q4-porthudson.png)
